issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaks into core/setup.py install_requires, propagating a CI-only workaround to every downstream user.
issues.detail: The mmcv/pkg_resources problem is a build-time CI issue. Adding setuptools<82 to core/setup.py install_requires forces every autogluon.core user to accept a capped setuptools forever, complecting a transient upstream bug with runtime environments. Scope the pin to the CI scripts or a build-only extra where the FIXME already lives.

issues.description: mmdet silently bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 with no justification in the diff.
issues.detail: The PR is framed as a mmengine/setuptools fix, but mmdet also moves a minor version. This is a second change riding a bug fix. If 3.3.0 is required for compatibility with mmengine 0.10.7 / mmcv 2.1.0, state it in a comment; otherwise split it so future rollback isn't guesswork.

issues.description: Switch from mim to pip with --no-build-isolation is undocumented and silently couples to ambient setuptools.
issues.detail: mim previously resolved prebuilt wheels matched to torch/CUDA. Plain pip with --no-build-isolation forces a source build that depends on the ambient setuptools<82 — the actual mechanism of the workaround. A one-line comment stating this precondition would let the next maintainer reason about removing it when upstream is fixed.

issues.description: FIXME comments cite mmcv#3325 but lack a revert condition or owner.
issues.detail: The FIXMEs reference the upstream issue but don't state what flips the cap off (e.g., mmcv ships a release that builds against setuptools>=82) nor who owns checking. Six months on, someone greps FIXME and has to reverse-engineer the trigger. Add the explicit revert criterion.

synthesis.summary: Panel consensus: NEEDS-WORK but narrow. The CI fix itself — pin setuptools<82 to dodge mmcv 2.1.0's pkg_resources build failure and install mmengine from PyPI — is reasonable and honestly labeled with FIXMEs. The main objection, unanimous across all three reviewers, is altitude: the same setuptools cap was added to core/setup.py install_requires, complecting a transient CI build constraint with every downstream user's runtime environment. Secondary concerns also unanimous: an unexplained mmdet 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 bump bundled into the fix, an undocumented mim-to-pip switch with --no-build-isolation, and FIXMEs that lack explicit revert criteria. Scope the pin to CI, justify or split the mmdet bump, and document the build-isolation precondition.
